title: TLS and TrustManager Bypass in Network Callbacks
platform_conditions: javax.net.ssl on JVM and Android runtime (API level 1+ for SSLSocketFactory/X509TrustManager; Network Security Config requires API 24+)
security_mechanism: A custom X509TrustManager whose checkServerTrusted body is empty (or only logs) makes every certificate chain accepted, so a machine with a hostile network position — attacker AP, compromised router, malicious proxy — terminates TLS invisibly; a HostnameVerifier returning true removes the hostname match the same way. This is usually added to silence a self-signed-certificate exception in debug and then shipped. Because the trust decision is inside the app, TLS loses its endpoint-authentication property entirely: tokens, session cookies, and user data flow in plaintext to the attacker while the UI still shows a secure connection.

source_sink_clues.source: The network position itself: any response the attacker substitutes on the path between device and server, accepted because the app disabled chain and hostname validation.
source_sink_clues.sink: sslSocketFactory(untrustedFactory, trustAllManager) / hostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true } / X509TrustManager with empty checkServerTrusted / SSLSocketFactory created from a null-trust SSLContext; cleartext http:// endpoints enabled via usesCleartextTraffic or an ATS-style networkSecurityConfig exception

tracking_guards: Check the installed trust manager actually verifies the chain and throws on failure (or that no custom manager is installed at all); check HostnameVerifier is absent or delegates to the default; check network security config does not blanket-disable cleartext or add user-added CAs for release builds; check certificate pinning (CertificatePinner / networkSecurityConfig pins) for high-value endpoints.
not_candidate_when: The trust-all factory is confined to unit tests or debug variants and cannot ship in release builds, the custom manager genuinely validates the chain against a pinned set (self-signed pinning is a legitimate use), or the endpoint carries no secret and only fetches public static content.
public_references: Android developer documentation: Network Security Config — https://developer.android.com/training/articles/security-config.html
